expected.claim: Both sub-cases reach the identical R3 recovery: the on-disk bytes are preserved byte-for-byte at a .corrupt-<timestamp> sibling, then `path` is overwritten with defaults.
expected.whyTheyAreOneDimension: ConfigManager.init wraps `decoder.decode(AppConfig.self, from: data)` in the *same* do/catch as the JSON parse itself (source lines 86-142) -- Swift's JSONDecoder throws a DecodingError for a present-but-wrong-typed field exactly the way it throws for unparseable bytes, and both land in the one catch block. There is no second, different recovery path for a type mismatch.

notes: This sub-case was found missing, not just unfixtured: the pre-P5.23 Rust `load_app_config` returned a bare `Err(AppConfigLoadError::Decode(_))` for a wrong-typed field with no backup/defaults recovery at all -- a real fidelity gap against the Swift source above, only visible by reading ConfigManager.init directly rather than trusting the JSON-syntax-only fixture P5.6 already had. Closed in this same step in crates/msc-infrastructure/src/config_repository.rs (load_app_config's new decode-error branch), since a dimension this step is explicitly asked to characterize with an executable case can't be characterized against behavior that doesn't yet exist. See that function's own doc comment.
